content.title: We're tracking all games, perfect brackets in the 2026 NCAA tournament
content.text: Sort By:Oldest FirstLatest4:40 am, March 28, 2026 The final Elite Eight ticket has been punched. No. 6 Tennessee took down No. 2 Iowa State, 76-62, to advance to its third straight Elite Eight. And the Volunteers did so by dominating the Cyclones in the second half in Chicago. It was tightly contested in the first half, with Tennessee taking a 34-33 advantage heading into the break. But the Volunteers separated themselves in the second half, going up by as many as 14 in second half. The double-digit deficit forced Iowa State to scramble as it tried to mount a late comeback, but the Cyclones, despite beginning to hit shots in the final minutes, could not overcome a poor shooting day that saw them go 39 percent from the field, 22 percent from 3 and 60 percent (15 of 25) from the free throw line. Tennessee dominated Iowa State on the boards, which was evident from the beginning of the game and reflected on the scoreboard as the contest moved along. The Volunteers finished with a 43-22 rebounding advantage, including a 16-8 advantage on the offensive boards. The Volunteers had four double-digit scorers, led by Nate Ament (18 points), Ja’Kobi Gillespie (16 points) and a double-double from Felix Okpara (12 points, 10 rebounds). Iowa State, playing without senior Joshua Jefferson who was injured in the second round, saw another NCAA tournament finish in the Sweet 16. The Cyclones had two double-digit scorers with Tamin Lipsey and Nate Heise finishing with 18 points apiece. The Cyclones had just three bench points. With the victory, Tennessee advanced to play No. 1 Michigan in the Elite Eight Sunday. Despite making their third Elite Eight appearance in as many years, the Volunteers are still searching for their first Final Four appearance. Bracket Tracker: Just 7.36 percent of Men’s Bracket Challenge brackets had the Volunteers advancing to the Elite Eight. Even fewer — just 1.90 percent — have them moving on to the Final Four. 4:16 am, March 28, 2026 UConn is moving on. No. 2 UConn held off No. 3 Michigan State, 67-63, to advance to the Elite Eight for the 14th time in program history. This game couldn’t have started much better for UConn, which went on a 22-2 run early to build a 19-point lead midway through the first half. Michigan State went on a run of its own to pull within eight by halftime, and that momentum carried over for the Spartans in the second half, as they went on a 16-2 spurt to pull within one early in the second half. The midway point of the second half saw Michigan State briefly take the lead, but the shots stopped falling for the Spartans in the second half as UConn, powered by the three-headed monster of Tarris Reed Jr. (20 points), Alex Karaban (17 points, seven rebounds) and Solo Ball (12 points), went up seven with just over five minutes to go. But Michigan State had a balanced scoring attack of its own with four players finishing in double figures, with Carson Cooper, Coen Carr and Jaxon Kohler finished with 14, 13 and 12, respectively. Jeremy Fears Jr., who struggled from the field most of the game (5 of 15) came through with a clutch 3-pointer and a pair of free throws in the final two minutes, twice pulling the Spartans within one. But it was the veteran Huskies in Karaban and Reed Jr., who hit a combined three free throws to extend UConn's lead to the four points it would win by in the final seconds, putting a stop to what could have been one of the largest comebacks in NCAA tournament history. UConn will play the No. 1 overall seed Duke in the Elite Eight on Sunday. Bracket Tracker: Of the Men's Bracket Challenge Game brackets, 48.76 had UConn advancing to the Elite Eight. Just 13.22 percent of brackets have the Huskies moving on to the Final Four. 1:59 am, March 28, 2026 Michigan is back in the Elite Eight for the first time since 2021. No. 1 Michigan won, 90-77, over No. 4 Alabama, becoming the third No. 1 seed this tournament to advance to the regional final. Alabama jumped out to a nine-point lead out the gate, but Michigan settled in and the two powerhouses went back-and-forth in a high scoring first half that saw 96 combined points. Michigan flipped the script in the second half, jumping out to an early lead it would grow to as many 16 points and would remain in double digits the remainder of the game. After scoring 49 first half points, Alabama finished with just 28 second half points. The Wolverines were efficient shooting the ball, shooting 50 percent from the field and 48 percent on 3s. Despite struggling from the free throw line (55 percent; 11-for-20), the Wolverines won comfortably. Michigan’s size proved to be a difference down the stretch. The Wolverine’s held a 46-32 advantage in the rebounding department. Michigan had four double-digit scorers, including a 23-point, 12-rebound and seven-assist double-double from Yaxel Lendeborg. Trey McKenney, Elliot Cadeau and Roddy Gayle Jr. finished with 17, 17 and 16 points, respectively. Alabama fell short in what could’ve been its third straight Elite Eight appearance. The Crimson Tide finished with 77 points, well below its NCAA-best average of 91.6 points per game. The Crimson Tide, who shot 36 percent from the field and 30 percent from 3, were led by a 35-point, seven-rebound, four-assist performance from Labaron Philon Jr. Latrell Wrightsell added 15 points while Aiden Sherrell had 10. Bracket Tracker: Michigan was selected in 77.95 percent of Men's Bracket Challenge brackets to make the Elite Eight, the most of any team. 1:26 am, March 28, 2026 Duke’s back in the Elite Eight. No. 1 Duke rallied to defeat No. 5 St. John’s, 80-75, to reach its 26th Elite Eight in program history. St. John’s gave Duke everything it could’ve wanted in what quickly became a Sweet 16 classic. The Red Storm and the Blue Devils exchanged runs throughout the game. Duke pulled ahead early but St. John’s hit timely 3-pointers each time Duke looked to be pulling ahead. Ruben Prey came off the bench for the Red Storm, hitting a trio of 3-pointers in the first half — he was 4 of 4 from 3 on the day — including a deep ball to give St. John’s the 40-39 halftime lead. St. John’s came out like a team on a mission in the second half, forcing turnovers and going on a 15-1 run early in the second half to go up by 10. But Duke, the No. 1 overall seed in this year’s tournament, would storm back to make it a one-possession game just a few minutes later. Isaiah Evans put the Blue Devils on his back, scoring a game-high 25 points while Cameron Boozer (20 points, 10 rebounds) hit key shots in the final moments to pull Duke ahead late. Caleb Foster, playing in his first game since fracturing his foot against North Carolina on March 7, added 11 points off the bench. The 3-pointers stopped falling for the Red Storm, who finished 13 for 32 from 3 after hitting nine deep balls in the first half. Duke, which struggled from 3 (36 percent), went 54 percent from the field and converted 15 of 24 free throws, taking a lead with 3:54 left in the game that it would not give up. St. John's had four players in double digits, led by Zuby Ejiofor (17 points, eight rebounds, six assists) and Bryce Hopkins (15 points, seven rebounds). Bracket Tracker: The people's favorite national champion escaped another scare. 77.18 percent of Men's Bracket Challenge brackets had Duke in the Elite Eight. Among brackets, the Blue Devils are the favorites to reach the Final Four (61.2 percent) and win the national title (25.15 percent). 4:20 am, March 27, 2026 Arizona showed why it’s a national title front-runner. No. 1 Arizona dominated No. 4 Arkansas, 109-88, clinching its first Elite Eight appearance since 2015. The Wildcats led from beginning to end, building a double-digit lead midway through the first half and never looking back. Arizona led Arkansas by as many as 25. Through three NCAA tournament games, Arizona has not trailed at any point. Arizona shot only eight 3s, making five, but shot an incredible 64 percent (37 for 58) from the field and 77 percent (30 for 39) from the free throw line en route to its dominating victory. All five of Arizona’s starters scored between 14 and 23 points, led by Brayden Burris (23 points) and Koa Peat (21 points). Arkansas’ superstar freshman Darius Acuff Jr. did what he could, scoring 28 points, including an 11 for 14 mark from the free throw line, while Meleek Thomas had 17 points and Billy Richmond III added 13. As a team, the Razorbacks struggled from 3 (22 percent) and shot a respectable 48 percent from the field and finished slightly below the 95.5 points they averaged in the NCAA tournament coming into the game. This win marks Arizona’s 12th Elite Eight appearance. The Wildcats are seeking their first Final Four appearance since 2001. No. 1 Arizona will play No. 2 Purdue Saturday. Bracket Tracker: 71.51 percent of Men’s Bracket Challenge brackets had Arizona advancing to the Elite Eight. 4:09 am, March 27, 2026 It’ll be an all-Big Ten Elite Eight in the South region. No. 3 Illinois pulled away to beat No. 2 Houston, 65-55, giving the Fighting Illini a matchup with No. 9 Iowa in the Elite Eight. This game started slow, with a combined two points in the first four-and-a-half minutes. Illinois led at halftime, 24-22, in the lowest scoring first half of this year’s NCAA tournament. But the Fighting Illini ensured that trend wouldn’t continue in the second half, going on a 17-0 run to put them up 18 points midway through the second half as Houston suffered a near seven-minute stretch without a point. Illinois shot 43 percent from the field and 39 percent from 3. The Fighting Illini were led by double-doubles from David Mirkovic (14 points, 10 rebounds) and Keaton Wagler (13 points, 12 rebounds) to go along with 13 points off the bench from Andrej Stojakovic. Houston began to get the basket to fall down the stretch, pulling within seven in the final minute, but couldn't overcome a rough shooting day. The Cougars went 34 percent from the field and 28 percent from 3. The Cougars, who average just under 16 free throw attempts per game, went just 2 for 2 from the free throw line, shooting their first and only free throws at the 3:27 mark in the second half. The Cougars were led by Emanuel Sharp (17 points) and Kingston Flemings (11 points). With the win, Illinois advances to its 11th Elite Eight in program history, its first since 2024, where it fell to eventual champion UConn. Illinois last made the Final Four in 2005 when it advanced to the national championship. Bracket tracker: Despite being a 3-seed, just 22.14 percent of Men’s Bracket Challenge brackets had Illinois advancing to the Elite Eight. 60.76 percent of brackets had Houston advancing. 1:34 am, March 27, 2026 Welcome back to the Elite Eight, Purdue. No. 2 Purdue outlasted No. 11 Texas, 79-77, in the Sweet 16 to advance to its seventh Elite Eight in program history and third since 2019. A go-ahead tip-in from veteran Trey Kaufman-Renn with 0.7 seconds kept Purdue's postseason hopes alive in a game where neither team held greater than a four-point advantage in the second half. The Boilermakers set the tone to start the game as Fletcher Loyer hit back-to-back 3-pointers to give them the 6-0 advantage. Loyer would hit two more 3s in the game and finished tied with 18 points, making all four of the Boilermakers' 3s, with other Purdue players combining to shoot 0 for 12 from deep. Purdue did most of its damage inside, led by Kaufman-Renn (20 points, eight rebounds), Braden Smith (16 points, five assists) and Oscar Cluff (11 points points, six rebounds). All five of Purdue's starters finished in double figures and all but four of 79 points came from its starting lineup. Unlike Purdue, Texas had a strong day from behind the arc, going 11 of 25 (44 percent) as a team. The Longhorns were powered by a season-best 29 points from Tramon Mark, who went 11 for 15 from the field and 5 for 7 from 3. Dailyn Swain added 15 points and nine rebounds while Jordan Pope had a 12-point game. Purdue ended the regular season going 6-7, but has looked every bit like a national championship contender since the start of the Big Ten tournament. The Boilermakers are still seeking their first NCAA tournament championship. Bracket Tracker: Purdue was the eighth-most picked team to advance to the Elite Eight, with 43.07 percent of Men's Bracket Challenge brackets picking the Boilermakers to advance past the Sweet 16. 1:25 am, March 27, 2026 How about those Hawkeyes? No. 9 Iowa delivered another upset, knocking off No. 4 Nebraska, 77-71. Perhaps the most surprising team left in this tournament, Iowa is moving on to its first Elite Eight appearance since 1987. The Hawkeyes keep finding a way to close out games, this time dispatching Big Ten rival Nebraska in the final minutes to end the Huskers' dream season. Iowa was led by Bennett Stirtz (20 points) and had a pair of double-digit performances from Alvaro Folgueiras (16 points) and Tate Sage (19 points) off the bench. The Hawkeyes trailed by as many as 10 in the first half and were behind a majority of the second half, but tied the game with just under three minutes to go. Iowa took the lead with 2:10 to go, outscoring Nebraska 20-9 down the game's final stretch. They're certainly no Cinderella, but the Hawkeyes have been perhaps the biggest surprise of the tournament, knocking off reigning national champion Florida in the second round on a corner 3-pointer in the final seconds. Iowa is now one win away from advancing to its first Final Four since 1980. Nebraska, which won its first NCAA tournament game in program history only a week ago, saw its season come to an end after going cold from the field in the final minutes. The Cornhuskers were led by a 25-point performance from Pryce Sandfort and a 16-point game from Braden Frager. Bracket Tracker: Didn't have Iowa in your Elite Eight? You're not alone. Just 2.02 percent of Men's Bracket Challenge brackets had the Hawkeyes in the Elite Eight. 2:32 pm, March 26, 2026 If you missed out on some of the Sweet 16 teams in your bracket, don't worry. Pretty much everyone did. Only 11 brackets out of the millions in the Men's Bracket Challenge Game correctly picked all Sweet 16 teams. That's fewer than last year, when 113 got all 16 right. Most brackets got between nine and 12 teams right, as 70.609 percent of MBCG brackets landed in that window. Though seven of the top eight teams are still left, No. 9 Iowa knocked out defending national champion and No. 1 Florida — and all four top seeds made the Sweet 16 in both 2024 and 2025. No. 11 Texas also went from the First Four to the Sweet 16. Those Hawkeyes and Longhorns are the biggest reasons why brackets missed some Sweet 16 teams. Only 5.64 percent had Iowa in the Sweet 16 and only 5.52 percent had Texas making the second weekend. On the opposite end, No. 1 Duke made it this far on 92.31 percent of brackets. Here's the rundown of the percent of brackets that got Sweet 16 teams correct: 0 out of 16: 0.482% 1 out of 16: 0.249% 2 out of 16: 0.443% 3 out of 16: 0.756% 4 out of 16: 1.373% 5 out of 16: 2.345% 6 out of 16: 3.679% 7 out of 16: 5.881% 8 out of 16: 9.945% 9 out of 16: 19.029% 10 out of 16: 19.123% 11 out of 16: 18.770% 12 out of 16: 13.687% 13 out of 16: 3.712% 14 out of 16: 0.506% 15 out of 16: 0.020% 16 out of 16: 0.0002% 4:03 am, March 23, 2026 The 3-pointers kept falling as No. 4 Alabama rolled No. 5 Texas Tech, 90-65, to reach the Sweet 16. The Crimson Tide hit 19 3-pointers on the night and never were challenged by the Red Raiders. Latrell Wrightsell sank six 3-pointers to score a game-high 24 points. He was one of seven Alabama players to make a 3-pointer, including Houston Mallette and his five 3-pointers. Alabama is in the Sweet 16 for the fourth consecutive year and will play top-seeded Michigan in Chicago. 3:26 am, March 23, 2026 Alex Karaban's career night lifted No. 2 UConn into the Sweet 16 and past UCLA, 73-57. Karaban scored a career-high 27 points on 9 for 16 shooting, making four 3-pointers. The Huskies trailed early but eventually separated themselves from UCLA. UConn held UCLA to only 39 percent shooting and won the rebounding battle 36-24. 78.36 percent of Men's Bracket Challenge Game entries had the Huskies in the Sweet 16, where they will take on No. 3 Michigan State. 2:30 am, March 23, 2026 Top-seeded Arizona withstood an offensive slump and second half Utah State push to become the third No. 1 seed to reach the Sweet 16, winning 78-66. It's the third year in a row the Wildcats are in the Sweet 16. The Wildcats, who led by as many as 18 points, saw their lead dwindle down to four before regrouping late to advance. Four players scored in double figures for the top seed, with Koa Peat (14 points, 10 rebounds) and Motiejus Krivas (11 points, 14 rebounds) both posting a double-double. Garry Clark scored 13 off the bench for the Aggies, who were attempting to reach the Sweet 16 for the first time since 1970.
